headline: The bounce failed: the VIX curve inverted, high yield gapped 11bp wider, and semis dragged the tape down — yet equal-weight still refuses to break.
summary: Yesterday's rotation was not a bottom. SPX -1.0% to 7,340.5, Dow -1.6%, Russell -1.5%, and the cash ETF tape through 16-Nov was uglier than the index: SPY -1.9%, QQQ -2.7%, SMH -5.1%. The vol complex finally repriced the front end: VIX 25.46, +11.1% on the day and +30.8% on the week (z=1.02), VIX3M 24.98, and VIX/VIX3M at 1.0192 — inverted, 76th percentile, the first time in this drawdown fear is priced in the next 30 days rather than the next quarter. SKEW is the tell on positioning: 145.1, -13.9% on the month at z=-2.10. Nobody owns tails; the damage is in the body of the distribution, which is exactly how forced de-grossing looks. Risk regime -17, credit & vol composite -31.

The epicentre is back where it started, and it is the AI capex chain. SMH -14.4% on the month and SOXX -24.2% over three; MU -7.6%, TSM -6.3%, ASML -5.9%, AMD -5.6% on the day; NVDA -27.1% in a month, 0th percentile of the 52-week range and 23.4% below its 200-day. GOOGL -4.1% and -16.7% on the month at z=-2.20. The power/electrification satellites are worse: GEV -17.1%, ETN -13.6%, VST -14.4%, GRID -8.1%, NLR -9.7% on the month. Nasdaq/S&P sits at the 10th percentile and growth/value is at the 1st percentile of the year (z=-2.26). But the index is not the market: equal-weight/cap-weight z=2.68 with acceleration 1.84, RSP +2.3% on the month against SPX -4.2%, and transports/S&P z=2.40 with acceleration 1.80. This is a de-rating of one crowded trade, not a growth scare in the broad tape.

What actually changed today is credit. HY OAS +11bp to 3.34 — the first meaningful daily widening of this episode — with IG at 0.90 and BBB at 1.12, both z=0.77, and CCC at 13.10 after +292bp in three months at the 91st percentile. HYG -0.3%, HYG/IEF -0.5%. It is a crack, not a break (HY is still only +3bp on the month, BKLN at the 95th percentile), but the direction is new. Rates stay the primary pressure: composite -53, real 10-year 2.92% (+26bp in a week, +48bp in three months, 29% above its 200-day) against a 10-year breakeven of 2.21% at the 9th percentile and a 5-year at 2.26%. That is a real-rate squeeze with disinflation underneath — the worst possible mix for long-duration equity. The small comfort: 2s and 5s fell 5bp, 10s 3bp; the front end is starting to price relief.

The dollar remains the wrecking ball but lost a notch of momentum. DXY 103.66 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.0993 at the 0th, USDCHF and USDCAD both at the 100th. USDBRL is still the most extreme print on the board at 5.7778, +14.1% on the month, z=3.97 with acceleration 2.97 — but it fell 0.1% today, and KRW, MXN and INR all firmed 0.5%. First day the EM-FX squeeze didn't extend. EWZ is down 26.1% on the month (z=-3.37) versus Bovespa -17.3%; that gap is pure currency. The offsets are real and getting cheaper to own: gasoline -22.7% and WTI -15.6% on the month feeding UPS +16.4% and FDX +11.6%; mortgage rates at 7.11%, -29bp with acceleration z=-2.36, feeding ITB +8.1%; XLV relative strength +9.7% on the month and XLF +4.8%. Labour is not the problem — claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%.

good.text: Breadth is still the strongest signal on the board and it is bullish: equal-weight/cap-weight z=2.68 with acceleration 1.84 and +5.5% on the month, RSP +2.3% while SPX fell 4.2%. The index damage is concentrated, not systemic.
Fuel deflation is paying transports: gasoline -22.7% and WTI -15.6% on the month, with IYT/SPY z=2.40 and acceleration 1.80, UPS +16.4%, FDX +11.6%, JETS +12.3%. IYT closed green on a -1.9% SPY day.

The inflation composite is +33 and genuinely easing: 10-year breakevens 2.21% (9th percentile), DBC z=-2.24, and 30-year mortgages at 7.11%, -29bp with acceleration z=-2.36 — which is why home construction is +8.1% on the month against a falling market.
The real economy is not rolling over: initial claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile of the year, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), retail sales running +6.8% y/y, unemployment down to 4.1%.

Defensives and financials are leading, not just hiding: XLV +6.3% on the month with relative strength +9.7%, LLY +14.0%, XLP at the 100th percentile, XLF +4.8% with rs +8.1%, KIE z=1.01, KRE/SPY z=0.93 with acceleration 1.06.

EM FX ex-Brazil stabilised for the first time in two weeks: USDKRW, USDMXN and USDINR all -0.5%, and USDBRL -0.1% after +14.1% on the month. The dollar squeeze stopped broadening even with DXY at the 100th percentile.

bad.text: Volatility regime change: VIX 25.46 (+11.1% day, +30.8% week), VIX3M 24.98, and the term structure at 1.0192 — inverted at the 76th percentile. With SKEW at 145.1 and z=-2.10, there are no tail hedges on to cushion a gap.

Semis accelerated lower, not higher: SMH -5.1% and -14.4% on the month, SOXX -5.4%, MU -7.6%, TSM -6.3%, ASML -5.9%; NVDA -27.1% in a month at the 0th percentile and 23.4% below its 200-day. Semis/S&P z=-1.97.
Credit finally participated: HY OAS +11bp to 3.34 (84th percentile), IG 0.90 and BBB 1.12 both at z=0.77, CCC 13.10 after +292bp in three months. HYG/IEF -0.5%. The last holdout started to go.

The real-rate squeeze is intact: 10-year TIPS 2.92%, +26bp on the week and 29% above its 200-day (z=0.63, acceleration +0.36), 2-year +27bp on the week, MOVE 101.9 and +10.2% on the week. Falling nominals today were all breakevens, not relief.

The dollar is still choking everything priced off it: DXY at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.0993 at the 0th, USDCHF and USDCAD at the 100th, CEW -1.4% on the month, USDBRL z=3.97 with acceleration 2.97.

Cyclicals and collateral assets keep confirming a liquidation, not a rotation: copper -8.2% on the month, COPX -5.4% on the day and -18.1% on the month, FCX -6.8%, XME -4.1%, CAT z=-2.49, plus BTC -21.2%, COIN -30.8%, MSTR -24.7% and gold at the 0th percentile.

trades.name: Short beta into an inverted vol curve
trades.line: Short SPHB vs long SPLV: vol curve inverted, de-gross the beta
trades.expr: Equal dollars: short SPHB, long SPLV. Options alternative: SPX one-month 7,100/6,700 put spread financed by selling the 7,700 call.
trades.thesis: The front of the vol curve inverted on the same day credit widened. In that regime beta compression runs further than it feels like it should: SPHB/SPLV is -12.4% on the month at z=-1.97 but still only the 22nd percentile of the last year, and SPLV is at the 99th.
trades.trigger: VIX +11.1% to 25.46 with VIX/VIX3M at 1.0192; HY OAS +11bp to 3.34; SPHB -3.7% versus SPLV -0.1% on the session; momentum factor MTUM -3.3% and z=-1.94.
trades.stop: VIX term structure back under 0.95 and HY OAS back below 3.20; or the ratio up 5% from entry.
trades.target: SPHB/SPLV toward 1.50, roughly 8% on the pair.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH: software/semis ratio z=1.59, turning up
trades.expr: Equal dollars long IGV, short SMH. Cleaner with options: long IGV Jan calls versus long SMH Jan puts, delta-matched.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is de-rating from the capex-heavy end first. Hardware carries the inventory, the cycle and the Taiwan concentration risk; software carries none of it and is still only 5.1% off on the month versus 14.4% for SMH. IGV/SMH is +24.8% over three months with acceleration 0.94 and only the 46th percentile of the year.
trades.trigger: SMH -5.1% versus IGV -2.2% on the session; MU -7.6%, TSM -6.3%, ASML -5.9%; SMH 11.9% below its 200-day while IGV sits 5.1% above its own.
trades.stop: Ratio -6%, or SMH reclaiming its 200-day with SOXX relative strength turning up.

trades.name: Credit catch-down
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF: HY OAS +11bp, the first real crack
trades.expr: Short HYG against long IEF, dollar-for-dollar; or buy HYG January puts roughly 3% out of the money.
trades.thesis: Credit has lagged the equity and vol repricing all month. The low-quality tail already moved — CCC 13.10 after +292bp in three months at the 91st percentile — while the HY index held at 3.34. With VIX at 25.46 and the curve inverted, index spreads catch down to the tail.
trades.trigger: HY OAS +11bp on the day, the largest single-day widening in the series; IG to 0.90 and BBB to 1.12, both z=0.77; HYG -0.3% and HYG/IEF -0.5% while IEF gained 0.2%.
trades.stop: HY OAS back under 3.20 with HYG/IEF making a new high; pair loss of 2.5%.
trades.target: HY OAS 3.90-4.00; roughly 4% on the pair.

trades.name: Fuel deflation: transports over energy
trades.line: Long IYT vs short XLE: fuel -23% on the month, IYT/SPY z=2.4
trades.expr: Equal dollars long IYT, short XLE. Single-name version: long UPS and FDX against short XOP.
trades.thesis: A 22.7% one-month collapse in gasoline and 15.6% in WTI is a direct margin transfer from producers to shippers, and it is already showing in the tape rather than being forecast. Transports/S&P has the second-highest acceleration on the board at 1.80.
trades.trigger: IYT +0.3% on a day SPY fell 1.9%; IYT/SPY z=2.40; UPS +16.4% and FDX +11.6% on the month with z of 2.08 and 1.22; XLE -2.0% and XOP -2.6% with crude z=-1.59 and rolling over.
trades.stop: Brent back above $100 (now 93.16) or XLE relative strength making new highs; pair -6%.

trades.name: Asia dispersion: India over Taiwan
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWT: India z=1.8 vs Taiwan z=-2.6
trades.expr: Equal dollars long INDA, short EWT. Size the short smaller if semis gap up; EWT already carries a 6.8% one-day loss.
trades.thesis: Taiwan is a levered semiconductor position with no domestic cushion; India is an oil-importing, domestic-demand market whose currency is appreciating. The crude collapse and the semi de-rating push these two in opposite directions at the same time.
trades.trigger: EWT -6.8% on the session, TAIEX -13.9% on the month at z=-2.61; INDA +8.2% on the month at z=1.81 with acceleration 1.24, Sensex z=2.31; USDINR -0.5% and -1.6% on the month.
trades.stop: Pair -7%, or SOXX reclaiming its 200-day (currently 12.0% below).

trades.name: Brazil: fade a four-sigma currency
trades.line: Long EWZ: z=-3.4 capitulation as USDBRL finally stalls
trades.expr: Buy EWZ outright at half size, or January calls roughly 5% out of the money. Add only on a second consecutive down day in USDBRL.
trades.thesis: EWZ is -26.1% on the month against Bovespa -17.3% — nine points of that is currency, not earnings. USDBRL at z=3.97 with acceleration 2.97 is the single most stretched print on the board, and four-sigma FX moves do not compound indefinitely.
trades.trigger: USDBRL -0.1% today after +14.1% on the month, the first stall; KRW, MXN and INR all -0.5%; Bovespa +0.3% with EWZ at the 3rd percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: USDBRL through 6.00, or EWZ -8% from entry.
trades.target: +15%, back toward the 200-day (EWZ is 16.0% below it).

trades.name: Gold over silver in a real-rate liquidation
trades.line: Long GLD vs short silver: ratio 81.8, z=1.68 and rising
trades.expr: Long GLD against short silver futures (or SLV), equal dollars. Ratio trade only — do not run it net long metals.
trades.thesis: This is a real-yield-driven liquidation of the entire precious complex, and the high-beta, margin-financed metal loses more in that regime. Gold/silver is +11.5% on the month at z=1.68 and the 99th percentile, and still well short of prior stress peaks.
trades.trigger: Real 10-year 2.92%, +26bp on the week and 29% above its 200-day; silver -8.6% on the week and -18.0% on the month versus gold -5.2% and -8.6%; platinum -8.1% on the week; GDX/gold -7.2%.
trades.stop: Ratio back under 76, or the 10-year real yield breaking below 2.75%; pair -4%.
